text: Adaptive Monte-Carlo Localization: a particle-filter method that finds the robot's pose in a map that already exists.
The coordinate frame rigidly attached to a mobile robot's base.
A multi-stage edge detection algorithm that uses Gaussian smoothing, intensity gradients, non-maximum suppression, and hysteresis thresholding to find thin, robust boundaries.
A plugin that adds one kind of information, such as lidar obstacles, to a costmap.
An electrostatic discharge vacuum cleaner used to clean accumulated dirt or dust inside the control box.
An annotated map that marks the areas a costmap filter acts on.
A formula, DOF = m(N − 1 − J) + Σfᵢ, that counts a mechanism's degrees of freedom from its number of links, joints and joint freedoms.
The costmap layer that adds extra cost around obstacles so the robot keeps its distance.
Joseph-Marie Jacquard's 1804 loom attachment that used chains of punched cards to control the woven pattern, an early example of a machine run by a stored program.
The Wireshark display filter protocol name for Modbus/TCP, defining fields including Transaction Identifier, Protocol Identifier, and Length.
An industrial communication protocol that carries Modbus messages over Ethernet, using port 502.
A robot motion command that interpolates the tool center point along a straight line in Cartesian space.
A world-fixed frame in which the robot's pose changes smoothly but slowly drifts.
A feedback control loop that calculates corrective motor commands by combining current error, accumulated past error, and the error's rate of change to hold a target speed or position.
A URScript function that combines two poses, used to convert a pose given in a feature or tool frame into the base frame, for example to compute an approach point.

Random Sample Consensus, an algorithm that finds geometric shapes (such as flat tables) in noisy point clouds by repeatedly testing random sample points against a distance threshold to ignore outliers.
A URScript command that reads a controller register and returns an integer value between 0 and 65535.
An axis position counter updated against a synchronization position marking in an ABB robot controller.
The Nav2 server that plans through a predefined graph of lanes and nodes, not through free space.
A control protocol for RC hobby servos where shaft angular position is proportional to a positive pulse width (1.0 ms to 2.0 ms) repeated every 20 ms (50 Hz).
A Nav2 plugin that takes a planned path and returns a smoother, improved one.
A program that is always in exactly one of a fixed set of states and moves to another state when a given event happens (also called a finite state machine).
Controlling a robot remotely in real time, as a surgeon does with the da Vinci system, so the robot follows a human operator rather than acting on its own.
The digital and analog inputs and outputs, plus switchable power, at a robot's wrist connector, used to drive and sense a gripper without cables along the arm.
The University of Michigan Benchmark, a calibration test where a robot drives clockwise and counter-clockwise square paths to separate and measure wheel diameter differences and wheelbase errors.
Using a camera and vision software to find where a part is, so the robot program can adjust its taught points to the part's actual position.
A classic PID tuning method that finds the gain at which the system oscillates steadily (Ku) and its period (Pu), then calculates starting values for Kp, Ki and Kd.
Build a ROS 2 Lyrical Python package from scratch: workspaces and overlays, ros2 pkg create, setup.py and package.xml, rosdep, colcon, and a timer-driven node that drives Turtlesim in a square.
Industrial camera sensors and optics: CMOS versus CCD, global and rolling shutters, pixel size and Nyquist resolution, focal length and f-number, telecentric lenses, and GenICam.
From discrete wiring to industrial networks: sinking and sourcing (NPN/PNP), fieldbus history, line, star and ring topologies, cyclic versus acyclic data, and Device Level Ring recovery.
